lesson_title: Draw It, Build It, Check It
hook_text: Two circuits, two breadboards, one habit: never put the battery on before you have checked the board against the drawing.
clip_script: Circuit one: 4.5 volt battery, switch, 470 ohms, LED, one loop, triangle toward minus. Trace it: 2.5 volts on the resistor, 2 on the LED, 5 milliamps, lit. Circuit two: 3 volts, a resistor and an LDR in a line with the middle going to a transistor base, buzzer from plus to collector. Dark pulls the base up, transistor on, buzzer sounds. Light pulls it down, quiet. Breadboard: rows of five, rails at the sides, long leg to plus. Finger on each part, match the diagram, then power. Dark? LED backwards first. Humming? Turn the divider. Write down what you measured next to what you predicted.
visual_style: Whiteboard LED loop with values; the LDR divider and transistor with a hand covering the LDR and a sound icon; a breadboard with rows highlighted; a checklist tick before a battery icon.
mood: Practical and confident, like a bench demonstration.
pacing: Loop, trace, divider, dark, breadboard, check, power, faults, record.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the LED circuit, then measure the volts across the resistor.
